- When sentiment turns negative in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecasted decline, cap the peak at 10–15% above recent high to avoid over-optimism.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (especially in first 10 days), apply a 3–5% downward bias to next period’s forecast.  
- When sentiment is uniformly positive for 5+ days, expect mean reversion within 7–10 days — adjust forecast to slightly lower than peak.  
- If forecasted price exceeds 85% of recent 30-day high, reduce by 5–8% to avoid overestimating volatility.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 75% of forecasted mean, apply a 2–4% downward correction to next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, expect volatility clustering — reduce forecast smoothness and add ±3% buffer.
